items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: Pops Foster was with Luis Russell, and everybody was taking lessons from him.

ctx.x: Those are the ones that migrated to Chicago, migrated from New Orleans around 1915, '16 and '17, and migrated from Chicago to Frisco and Oakland and San Diego. Jelly Roll and all of them went out there, when Watts was... They speak of Watts as a cowboy place, a country...you know, Western town.
That almost makes me the oldest one now standing. After you get past Garland and Pops Foster. I guess you ...(?)... and your day will come. There it is. You have to look at Bill Johnson...

items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Guitar player, Bill Johnson, used to get drunk, to the annoyance of Paul and Pops Foster. I’m there.

ctx.x: Which was the first band that you played with like that? The first big band?

First big band was Luis Russell. Guitar player, Bill Johnson, used to get drunk, to the annoyance of Paul and Pops Foster. I’m there. So Bill Johnson don’t show up or some [expletive deleted], so they send for me. But Luis Russell knew I’m a kid. He’s looking for names in his band. I don’t have no name, you understand? He’s looking for a name. He want to get Lee Blair, who had been with Jelly Roll, or Jeff Williams and different hell of a guitars players who had changed from guitar to banjo. I just had changed…
